subject: Support coverage & escalation playbook — MSA/order form redlines
messages:
From: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@acme.com>

Cc: legal@acme.com, ops@acme.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Initial redlines: uptime targets + maintenance windows

Hi Ben —

Thank you for the draft order form. Our legal and ops teams reviewed the SLA sections and have a few blocking items we need to resolve before procurement can sign:

- Uptime target: we need a minimum 99.95% rather than the proposed 99.9% for mission-critical routes.
- Service credits: the current credit tiering caps at 10% annual; our procurement requests a higher cap for sustained outages.
- Response times: we need P1 response within 30 minutes and a guaranteed on-call contact 24/7.
- Maintenance windows: clarify planned maintenance blackout windows and notice period (we ask for >= 72 hours notice for non-emergency maintenance).

I’ve attached the ACME redline PDF with inline commentary. Can you coordinate? Looping in ops/legal (copied).

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lopez
Head of Cloud Ops | Acme Cloud Services

Subject: Re: Initial redlines: uptime targets + maintenance windows

Hi all —

I reviewed ACME’s PDF and Ben’s MSA redlines. High level thoughts:

1) Uptime target: 99.95% vs 99.9% 
   - The delta materially increases cost/exposure on both sides. Proposed compromise: 99.92% for the first year with an objective review at the 12-month mark tied to usage metrics. Alternatively, grant 99.95% for a subset of critical routes (list to be defined) rather than platform-wide.

2) Service credits cap: 
   - We cannot agree to uncapped or very high annual credit exposure. Suggest moving from fixed annual cap to an exposure formula tied to monthly committed spend (e.g., max credit = min(25% of monthly committed spend, $X)). That preserves predictability.

3) P1 response / on-call contact:
   - We can commit to a 30-minute acknowledgement for P1s with an SLA-based severity matrix. For guaranteed 24/7 on-call, we can provide a single on-call channel and duty rotation; a named primary contact for escalation (for contractual purposes) is acceptable.

4) Maintenance notice:
   - 72 hours for non-emergency maintenance is reasonable for planned major changes. For routine patching we maintain a 48-hour notice window. We will mark emergency and security patches as exempt with immediate notifications and post-facto reporting.

I’ll produce specific line edits for the order form and the MSA, and propose redline language for the subset-of-routes approach. Please confirm Thu 6/22 11am PT for the sync.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
From: ops@acme.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: sarah.lopez@acme.com
Date: Thu, 22 Jun 2028 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines: uptime targets + maintenance windows

On Thu, Jun 22, 2028 at 11:00 AM Redwood Inference wrote:
> Confirming 11am PT — joining.

Thanks for the fast turn. A few clarifications from ACME ops after the sync:

- The request for 99.95% is specifically for our customer-facing inference endpoints (low-latency production fleet) — we can be flexible on internal/auxiliary services.
- If Redwood proposes a subset-of-routes approach, we’ll provide a list of endpoints we consider mission-critical within 2 business days.
- On service credit formula: ACME prefers a floor that allows meaningful remediation for multi-hour outages. The proposed formula tied to committed spend is OK — but the constant ($X) needs to be large enough to be meaningful for us.
- Regarding on-call: we prefer a named escalation path (primary and secondary) with guaranteed response within 30 minutes and a separate 2-hour remediation commitment for P1s.

We’ll send a short internal note with the exact endpoint list and suggested $X value later today.

—ACME Ops
